request: Fix the corpus delta-apply path, which silently degrades PlantUML diagram shards. When /archive applies a confirmed System delta row for an element that already has a shard, the caller of writeDiagramShard passes the element id as `label`, lets `technology` default to the kind, and passes `description: null` — so the rewritten shard loses the element's anchor path, its C4 techn value and its human title. Reproduced live during workflow consumer-install-defects (commit 79e41cb): docs/system/diagrams/audit-baseline-checks.puml went from `Component(audit_baseline_checks, ".claude/skills/audit-baseline/checks/*.mjs", "subsystem", "Per-surface baseline audit checks")` to `Component(audit_baseline_checks, "audit-baseline-checks", "c4_component")`, and consent-commands.puml the same way; both were held out of that commit and remain dirty in the working tree as the reproduction. Not a schema migration: 85 of 116 diagrams still carry the rich 4-argument form and 19 carry the degraded 3-argument form. Recurring, not a one-off: commit 0d8e776 (2026-08-09) degraded audit-baseline-helpers.puml and document-helpers.puml by the same path, so the damage accumulates one workflow at a time. Mechanism is at .claude/skills/workspace/shards.mjs:76 componentLine({label, technology, description}), which renders faithfully — the loss is entirely in its caller. Two deliverables: (1) the forward fix, so a rewrite preserves anchor, techn and description (or leaves an already-correct shard alone); (2) a decision on repairing the 19 already-degraded diagrams, including whether the restore is derivable from the element records under docs/system/elements/, which still hold anchor and title.
novelty_evidence: Searched docs/specs/, docs/archive/**/spec.md and .claude/memory/backlog/ for the shard field contract. The 2026-08-07 system-spec-delta-slice-b spec names writeDiagramShard but specifies none of technology/descr/subsystem, and no backlog entry or roadmap item covers it — the roadmap has one open task (T11, landmark scope re-homing), unrelated. The correct rewrite semantics are undefined anywhere on disk, which is why the defect could accumulate silently across at least two workflows.
track_reason: The leanest safe track is tdd-quickfix, and two facts make it insufficient. First, the correct field semantics are unspecified anywhere on disk, so the fix needs a written contract rather than only a passing test — the next caller of writeDiagramShard would otherwise face the same undefined behaviour. Second, repairing the 19 already-degraded diagrams is a data decision with corpus-wide blast radius: the comment at shards.mjs:68-74 records that 51 shards declare `subsystem` in the techn slot while their element record reads `kind: component`, and that this distinction exists nowhere else on disk, so a wrong repair destroys it permanently. Both want gate A. User confirmed spec-entry via AskUserQuestion.
